descriptionChirho: Proper noun designating the Mesopotamian city Sepharvaim (dual form), referenced in Assyrian conquest and resettlement narratives (2 Kgs 17:24, 18:34, 19:13; Isa 36:19, 37:13). All three clusters represent the same geographical referent in various syntactic positions: standalone, with conjunction waw, and a ketiv variant. Multilingual translations uniformly render it as a single toponym: Spanish 'Sefarvaim,' Hindi 'सफरवायिम / सपरवायिम,' Arabic 'سَفَرْوَايِمَ,' Korean '스바르와임 / 스발완임,' Swahili 'Sefarvaimu.' The ketiv reading S121334 is simply an orthographic variant of the same place name.
